messages.content: 我想在聖荷西附近的Walmart買蘋果、米飯和12罐瓶裝水。請顯示產品資訊和庫存情況。

function.name: walmart_purchase
function.description: Retrieve information of items from Walmart including stock availability. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

product_list.description: Items to be purchased listed in an array.

pack_size.description: Size of the product pack if applicable. The size of the array should be equal to product_list. Default is not use it if not specified.

The user wants to buy apples, rice, and 12 cans of bottled water near San Jose Walmart. They want product info and stock status. We need to call the function walmart_purchase with loc "San Jose" or maybe "nearby" but we can specify location as "San Jose". Provide product_list ["apples", "rice", "bottled water"] and pack_size [1,1,12] maybe? Actually pack_size array length equals product_list. For apples and rice default no pack size needed. But they want 12 cans of bottled water. So pack_size could be [null, null, 12] or just [12] for water? The function signature says pack_size?: number[]. The size of the array should be equal to product_list. So we need to provide pack_size array of same length. For apples and rice we can set 0 or 1? Not sure. Maybe we can omit pack_size entirely because it's optional. But the user specifically wants 12 cans of bottled water. So we might pass pack_size [12] only for water? But the spec says size of array should be equal to product_list. So we need to provide pack_size array of length 3. We can set pack_size [1,1,12] meaning one apple, one rice, twelve water. That seems fine.

We then call the function.
